theme.name: Outdated Concordat requires simplification
theme.claim: A scheduled review of the 2012 Concordat concluded that it contains elements no longer relevant to UK fisheries management and needs to be simplified to provide clarity to fishermen and government.

text.line: The four Administrations agreed, when the 2012 Concordat was adopted, that there would be a review of its operation to ensure that the Concordat remains relevant; that review has now been completed.

The review concluded that the existing Concordat contained elements which are no longer relevant in UK fisheries management and proposed changes to simplify and provide clarity to fishermen and government.

theme.name: Vessel mobility mismatches with licensing administration
theme.claim: Changes of ownership or business decisions mean vessels increasingly operate in and land into a different part of the UK than the Administration that licenses them, creating a need for clearer rules on moving between Administrations.

text.line: Whether for reasons of change of ownership or simply because of a business decision to pursue different fisheries, there will be reasons why vessels may wish to operate in a different constituent part of the UK.

theme.name: Economic link condition needs re-examination
theme.claim: The existing economic link licence condition, which permits foreign-owned quota holders access to UK waters in exchange for an economic link, needs review to ensure it delivers meaningful benefits to coastal communities.

text.line: The 2012 Concordat contains an economic link condition which allows for foreign access by other Member States to UK waters, where the holder of the quota has an economic link to the UK e.g. quota held by an operator based in another member state but who employs a UK crew.

theme.name: FQA trading creates tension with their legal status
theme.claim: Although FQA units confer no formal right to a share of UK quota, in practice they are traded and holders have a general expectation of receiving quota allocations, creating a management issue the Concordat must address.

text.line: Administrations acknowledge nonetheless that FQA holdings involve at present a general expectation of receiving a share of UK annual quotas.
Administrations also acknowledge that there is a trade in FQA units.
The Concordat is an agreement between all four fisheries administrations in the UK that sets out the broad principles that apply for the management of their own commercial fishing fleets.

The Concordat provides the flexibility for fisheries administrations to adopt their own management rules, whilst respecting certain overarching UK principles on quota, effort control and licencing regimes.
The UK Fisheries Administrations are individually responsible for the management of UK quota, which is divided between Administrations according to the UK quota management rules.
Until exit negotiations are concluded, the UK remains a full member of the European Union and all the rights and obligations of EU membership remain in force.
